preserved_v1_contract.objective: Create an ECG-triggered cardiac T2-prepared Cartesian bSSFP acquisition. Use a 40 ms T2 preparation with a 90-degree tip-down, two 180-degree refocusing pulses and a 90-degree tip-up, ending before imaging. Every acquired ADC sample must lie between 600 and 800 ms after its ECG R-wave trigger, using nominal RR 1000 ms on physio1; preparations may precede that window. Use ordinary Cartesian reconstruction. Complete magnetization preparation before the imaging window. Balance net gradient area on all three axes in every readout TR; alternate excitation RF phase by 180 degrees between readout TRs and keep receiver phases coherent with that RF phase cycle. Use symmetric echo timing in every acquired readout TR: TE is measured from the excitation RF center to the readout k-space-center echo, and abs(TE - TR/2) must be no more than max(0.01 ms, 0.05 times TR). For every nonzero T2 preparation, use exactly four separate RF events: a 90-degree tip-down, two 180-degree refocusers and a 90-degree tip-up. Measure preparation duration from tip-down RF center to tip-up RF center. Place the refocusing RF centers at one-quarter and three-quarters of that duration. Relative RF phases must be phi, phi + 90 degrees, phi + 90 degrees and phi + 180 degrees, respectively. Tip pulses must be within 2 degrees of 90; refocusers must reach at least 178 degrees of waveform-derived nominal flip. RF phase tolerances are 0.01 rad. Preparation duration and refocuser-center timing tolerances are twice the larger of the RF and block-duration rasters.
